title: stabilize-sse-offset-compaction-and-toolcall-affinity
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We continue to see downstream partial-JSON churn and fncall reordering when small SSE fragments arrive out-of-order or are interleaved with heartbeat delimiters. This causes user-visible truncated structured outputs and toolcall boundary mispairings in edge network conditions (mobile/poor NAT). This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: 1) offset compaction: a lightweight compaction ledger that coalesces adjacent tiny fragments in the in-memory fragment store before attempting final JSON reassembly, reducing reassembly thrash for high-fragmentation traces; 2) toolcall affinity heuristics: a pairing affinity window so function-call sentinel tokens are held and reassembled with preferred fragments rather than flushed when ambiguity exists. Additionally this change tightens delimiter anchoring rules so the parser prefers explicit sentinel anchors over ambiguous heartbeat delimiters during contention and introduces an idempotent reconnect checkpoint token emitted at a stable point in the stream to speed client resumption. Changes: - runtime/sse/framereader.go: add offset compaction map and compaction pruning based on configurable hysteresis (default 35ms) and size threshold to avoid waiting on long stalls. - runtime/sse/parser.go: introduce delimiter anchor preference ordering and affinity-aware reassembly path for fncall sentinels; add unit tests for ambiguous-delimiter sequences. - pkg/openai/compat/handler.go: emit reconnect checkpoint token and handle client resume requests; ensure compatibility with existing replay semantics. - internal/protocol/checkpoint.go: new idempotent token format and validation helpers. - tests/e2e/sse_stream_partial_json_test.go: new randomized fuzz cases that simulate interleaved heartbeats, reordered fragments, and mid-json splits; added deterministic seeds used in CI. - docs/streaming.md: document new hysteresis config and checkpoint semantics, and migration notes for Private deployments. Backwards compatibility: the reconnect checkpoint is opt-in via a small negotiation header to avoid surprising older clients; the default hysteresis is conservative to avoid added latency for well-behaved streams. Performance: microbenchmarks show a 28% reduction in reassembly retries and a 12% reduction in median tail latency for highly-fragmented traces in our lab harness. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for parser reassembly and delimiter anchoring - [x] e2e fuzz scenarios and deterministic seeds - [x] compatibility negotiation for checkpoint token - [x] documentation updates - [x] canary rollout plan in release notes Testing and rollout: CI runs include unit, integration, and the new e2e fuzz suite. We will ship as a staged canary: 5% hosted traffic for 24h, 25% for 48h, then 100% with automatic rollback on regression. Related work: builds on ENG-2142 (sse-cohesion-hysteresis) and ENG-2267 (fncall-order-preservation); incident SUP-9081 motivated the initial triage. Merge method: squash and merge with small follow-up hotfix expected for telemetry label normalization.

release_notes: Introduce SSE offset compaction and toolcall affinity to reduce partial-JSON truncations and preserve function-call ordering under high-fragmentation networks. Opt-in reconnect checkpoint token for faster client resumption. Backwards-compatible by default. Configurable hysteresis (default 35ms) available for tailoring to customer needs.
notes: Canary rollout scheduled; telemetry dashboard created in observability-pack to track compaction.* and affinity.evictions. Follow-up ticket ENG-2399 created to add zero-copy compaction path and Dedicated-tunable hysteresis.
